title: Phase 5 · Observe: See What Is Happening in Production
html:
Goal: going live is not the finish line. In this chapter you use the V3 console's observability dashboard, session replay and trace waterfall to find where an answer spent its time and how many tokens it burned. Then you use the Standards workbench's drift watch to re-apply the signed standard to lab-service-assistant on a schedule, and read the scorecard and decision history to answer "is the standard still holding, and who decided what".

Prerequisites

You need From
Release policy of workspace default set to gated (every invoke goes to the live endpoint) The Roles chapter
Criteria unicorn-service-criteria v1 (P1, P2, K1, C1, Q1, S1, S2) published and signed by biz-owner; golden set unicorn-service-golden serving it, curated 24 / 15 / 9 with holdout sealed The Define and Evaluate chapters
Deployed lab-service-assistant (with knowledge base lab-unicorn-policies) and lab-policy-advisor The Build chapter
The release gate has run on a candidate; S2 has a calibration decision (in this lab "not aligned") The Evaluate chapter
live of lab-service-assistant points at the released version N+1 (teams that skipped the re-release stay on the old version — this chapter works either way); Cedar policies on launchpad-gw switched to ENFORCE; API key console-1 The Release chapter

Accounts used in this chapter, and why:

Account Does Why
developer Generates test traffic, reads traces, configures and triggers the drift watch Editing the watch needs criteria.manage, triggering a run needs eval.run — engineering work
biz-owner Reads the dashboard, sessions, intent view and scorecard The business owner checks whether the standard holds but does not change schedules; in a fresh window their rail shows the everyday modules only
admin Reads spend & alerts, Gateway decision logs and the decision history GET /api/costs and GET /api/audit are admin-only (spend by person names individuals)

Observability data comes from CloudWatch Transaction Search (aws/spans). Spans land with a delay (in this lab the last answer's trace was still incomplete 10 seconds after it finished and fully visible 2.5 minutes later), so a trace you cannot see right after chatting is normal. Dashboard queries are cached for 60 seconds per (view, range); the right of the page header shows "cached Ns ago", and Refresh next to it forces a re-read.

1. Generate a little traffic

Sign in as developer, click Chat at the top of the rail (/v3/chat), pick lab-service-assistant in the Agent picker in the left column, click New conversation and send the questions below one at a time (wait for each answer):

text
I bought Bluetooth earbuds on Unicorn Mall and signed for them the day before yesterday. The box is open but the device is not activated. Can I still use the 7-day no-reason return?
I'm a Gold member and the order paid amount was ¥380. How soon do I get my refund after returning it?
Unicorn Air UC1208, Standard economy, fare ¥1,200, departing in three days. How much do I get back if I refund now?
Does Economy Lite include free checked baggage?
Unicorn Hotels Standard Prepaid rate, check-in 20 October, I cancel on 19 October at 10:00. How much is charged?

Switch the Agent picker to lab-policy-advisor (switching starts a new conversation) and send:

text
Can a flash-sale item use a platform coupon? Does the spend-threshold discount still stack?

Expected result: both agents answer; a tool row appears above each answer (kb_search for lab-service-assistant, plus calculator or current_utc_time when it works out money or time; skills and agentic-lab-policy-advisor___AgenticRetrieveStream for lab-policy-advisor), and every answer has two icon buttons, thumbs up / down (their labels are Good answer / Bad answer). Do not thumbs-down yet — the Improve chapter uses it. With live = v4 the answers cite policy rule ids (teams that skipped 1.6 of the Release chapter and stayed on v2 get no ids).

One observed answer per question (live = v4, model GLM-5.3; the chat time is from send to the end of the answer on the Chat page, the trace figures come from the session detail in sections 3 and 4):

Question Key points of one observed answer Chat time Tools Trace duration · spans · tokens
Opened, unactivated earbuds Within the window (R-01); electronics qualify for the 7-day no-reason return only with an intact factory seal and no activation (R-03): only the outer box opened and the seal intact → still returnable, factory seal broken → not; quality issues can be returned or exchanged within 15 days (R-04) 11.7 s kb_search × 2 6.6 s · 19 · 7,710
Gold member, ¥380 order Instant refund at pickup (R-07); wallet within 2 hours, debit card 1–3 working days, credit card 3–7 working days (R-08) 9.0 s — 8.8 s · 12 · 6,831
UC1208 Standard economy refund Fee 25% = ¥300 (A-03), taxes ¥80 refunded in full (A-06), you get ¥980 (A-07) 30.8 s kb_search × 2, calculator 31 s · 23 · 30,700
Economy Lite checked baggage 0 kg free checked allowance (A-12); buy online 24 hours ahead at ¥120 / 20 kg, ¥200 at the counter (A-14) 62.9 s — 63 s · 12 · 12,744
Standard Prepaid, cancel 19 Oct 10:00 28 hours before check-in, under 48 hours, first night charged (H-03), with the official ¥680/night example (H-10) 89.2 s kb_search × 2, current_utc_time 89 s · 23 · 38,332
Flash sale and platform coupon (lab-policy-advisor) Flash-sale items cannot use a platform coupon (R-11); the spend-threshold discount still stacks (R-10, R-11) 22.2 s skills, …___AgenticRetrieveStream 19 s · 32 · 10,099

These are the readings of one run and they vary a lot: in the previous walkthrough the same questions took 4–13 seconds. The five-question lab-service-assistant session used 96,317 tokens in total (89,439 in, 6,878 out), about $0.19; tokens grow turn by turn because every turn sends the earlier conversation and retrieval results to the model again (which is also where the Evaluate chapter's K1 of 6,799 tokens per session comes from).

V3's Chat page holds only the conversation, with no trace panel. Read the spans of these sessions under Observability → Sessions below; Open in chat on the session detail takes you back to Chat to continue the session.

2. Read the dashboard

In another browser window (a private window or another browser profile) sign in as biz-owner. In a fresh window a member account's rail shows the everyday modules only: the fixed entries at the top — Command center, Agents, Chat, Release gate — stay, and Modules keeps only Architect assistant, New agent, Knowledge Bases, Releases, Issue box, Observability, Intent view, Standards, Video introductions. Show every module at the bottom of Modules shows them all; it is a view filter, not authorization.

Click rail Modules → Agent runtime → Observability (/v3/observability); the Dashboard tab opens. Leave the time range to the right of the tabs at 24H (also: 1H, 6H, 7D).

In the image: 1 range 24H; 2 Needs a look: "P95 latency is 32s"; 3 the tiles Traces 171, Sessions 167, Error rate 0.0%, Latency P50 / P95 10s / 32s, Tokens 990K (≈$2.16); 4 the Traffic and Latency charts (latency peak 126s); 5 Tools (kb_search 217 calls and more) and Tokens by model (prices updated 2026-10-19).

Area How to read it
Needs a look The page leads with what stands out (a high error rate, an error spike, a slow P95, a failing tool); click one to jump to the matching traces. When nothing does it says "Nothing stands out across N traces." and the page title reads "Running clean"
Traces One invoke is one trace; the line below splits ok and failed
Sessions Sessions in range, plus the number of active agents
Error rate Turns red above 5%
Latency P50 / P95 Percentiles of the root span; many short requests pull them down
Tokens Total tokens, with input / output tokens and a ≈$ cost estimate below
Traffic Traces per bucket, errors on top
Latency Root-span P50 and P95 curves
Tools Calls and success rate per tool, failing first: kb_search / kb_deep_search of lab-service-assistant (generated code calling Bedrock retrieval on lab-unicorn-policies directly) and agentic-lab-policy-advisor___AgenticRetrieveStream of lab-policy-advisor (the retrieval tool on the knowledge base gateway)
Tokens (chart) Tokens and estimated cost per model; cost comes from a price map, not your bill

On cost: the bottom of the Tokens chart card names the price map (here price map: config/launchpad.yaml · model_prices · prices updated 2026-10-19). The map has global.zai.glm-5.3 (input 1.68, output 5.28 USD per million tokens), so GLM-5.3 cost shows as a ≈$ amount; a model missing from it shows tokens and — for cost. Update prices at the top right of that card rewrites the price map shared by the whole workspace, so it is shown only to administrators and members with project write access (project.write) — that is with a single project in the workspace; with several, only an administrator may change it. In this lab biz-owner's project role carries project.write, so the button shows; leave it to the administrator.

Expected result (measured in this lab, 24H):

  • The page title is 1 thing worth a look; Needs a look has 1 item: "P95 latency is 32s", with "Slow above 10s; a root span past 30s counts as a timeout." and a Traces link on the right.
  • Traces 171 (171 ok · 0 failed); Sessions 167 (7 active agents); Error rate 0.0% (0 of 171 traces); Latency P50 / P95 10s / 32s (shown in red); Tokens 990K (in 851K · out 139K · ≈$2.16).
  • The Traffic chart shows traces per bucket; the Latency chart reads "peak 126s" with the legend P50 · 10s and P95 · 32s. Latency is far above the fastest answers of section 1 because the 24 hours also include the evaluation runs, the A/B experiment and the canary replays of earlier chapters, and the model itself is fast at some times and slow at others.
  • Tools: kb_search 217 calls, calculator 17, kb_deep_search 7, current_utc_time 4, agentic-lab-policy-advisor___AgenticRetrieveStream 2, skills 1, all at 100%.
  • Tokens chart: global.zai.glm-5.3 990K · ≈$2.16 (every agent in this lab uses that model).

3. Replay a session

Switch to the Sessions tab. Filter the agent picker (default All agents) to lab-service-assistant; the filter next to it offers All / With errors / Clean, and Search a session id narrows further. Each row shows Session, Agent, Traces, LLM calls, Tokens · cost, Errors and Last active. After filtering, the first row (most recent Last active) is the five-question session from section 1: in this lab Traces 5, LLM calls 10, Tokens · cost 96,317 / ≈$0.187. Click it to open the session detail; its Conversation block starts with the user message "I bought Bluetooth earbuds on Unicorn Mall…".

In the image: 1 Open in chat, Score now and refresh; 2 tiles: Traces 5, LLM calls 10, Tokens 96,317 (in 89,439 · out 6,878), Est. cost ≈$0.187; 3 the Conversation replay (actor developer); 4 Traces in this session: five POST /invocations cards, the top one (89s) is the slowest.

The session detail has:

  • Header: the title is the agent name, the small line above it Session · <Session ID>, and below it the first-seen / last times. On the right: Open in chat (continues this session in Chat), Score now and a refresh button.
  • Tiles: Traces (with Copy id for the full Session ID), LLM calls, Tokens (in / out), Est. cost.
  • Conversation: turn-by-turn replay; the small line at its top right names the source (here agentcore memory · ListEvents · actor developer).
  • Traces in this session: one card per invoke with duration, spans, LLM calls, tokens and cost (here, newest first: 89s · 3 LLM · ≈$0.075, 63s · 1 · ≈$0.024, 31s · 3 · ≈$0.056, 8.8s · 1 · ≈$0.014, 6.6s · 2 · ≈$0.018). The card title is the root operation, POST /invocations. A multi-turn session has several cards — read them one by one rather than taking the session total as one answer's cost.
  • Online evaluation: appears only when the agent has an online evaluation config (the Improve chapter), with the evaluators' scores; with a config but no score yet it says "No online evaluation scored this session yet.". No online evaluation is configured at this point, so the block does not appear.
  • Score now: V3 has not rebuilt this; the button opens this session's full page inside V3 (address /v2/observability?…&full=1), with the Score now card further down.

Score now (developer):

  1. As developer, open the same session detail, click Score now and scroll to the Score now card (its title reads "0 of 5 evaluators selected"; the evaluator list has 35 entries over 4 pages).
  2. Type Helpfulness into the search box at the top right of the card and tick Helpfulness (Builtin.Helpfulness); then type privacy and tick unicorn_privacy_guard. Both judge the session alone and need no expected answer. unicorn_fee_check and unicorn_no_overpromise can be ticked too, but their rubrics reference {expected_response}, which a session does not have, so leave them out. Only Builtin.TrajectoryExactOrderMatch, Builtin.TrajectoryInOrderMatch and Builtin.TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch cannot be ticked; hovering shows "Needs ground truth — not available for on-demand session scoring" (/api/eval/evaluators returns requires_ground_truth for those three only).
  3. Click Score at the top right of the card; the "Score this session now?" dialog says "Runs 2 evaluator(s) over this session's spans — one billable judge inference per evaluator. Results are shown here and not persisted."; click Score in the dialog.

In the image: 1 the search box (use it to find and tick both evaluators; the card title then reads 2 / 5 evaluators selected); 2 the Score button; 3 the summary "122 spans sent · 10 results · not persisted"; 4 the results table: each evaluator scores each of the 5 traces once, Builtin.Helpfulness 0.83 / 1.00, unicorn_privacy_guard all pass.

Expected result (measured in this lab, back in about 25 seconds): below the card appear "122 spans sent · 10 results · not persisted" and a results table with the columns Evaluator, Score, Label, Explanation — click a row to expand, Tokens (in / out) and Status (all Scored). Both are trace-level evaluators, so each scores each of the 5 traces once: Builtin.Helpfulness measured 0.83 / 0.83 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.83 once (in question order; 1.00 carries the label Above And Beyond, 0.83 Very Helpful), and unicorn_privacy_guard gave all five 1.00 with label pass; each judge input was 5,513–17,106 tokens (later turns carry longer context in their traces). Scoring the same session again can differ slightly (another run in this lab gave three 1.00 and two 0.83). The results are not persisted; for scores you can keep and reproduce, use an evaluation run with the golden set.

Score now makes billed Bedrock calls and the route is open to every member. Following this workshop's split of duties, let developer press Score; biz-owner only reads.

4. Find the slow call in the trace waterfall

Back in biz-owner's session detail, under Traces in this session, click the card with the longest duration (each card reads duration · N spans · N LLM · N tokens · cost; compare the first number; in this lab it is the top card, 89s · 23 spans · 3 LLM · 38,332 tokens · ≈$0.075, the hotel cancellation question); or on the Observability page switch to the Traces tab and click the same trace.

In the image: 1 tiles: Duration 89s, Spans / LLM 23 / 3, Tokens 38,332, Est. cost ≈$0.075; 2 legend: LLM, Tool, Memory, HTTP, Agent; 3 the tool row kb_search (440ms, in parallel with a second retrieval); 4 the third model call chat global.zai.glm-5.3 (65s, the bulk of the time); 5 the Span card: model, finish reason, duration and tokens (input 18,488 · output 1,259 · ≈$0.038).

The header title is the root operation with its status (here POST /invocations · OK), and the small line below gives agent, start time and service name; Open session on the right goes back to the session. The tiles are Duration (with Copy id), Spans / LLM, Tokens and Est. cost. The Waterfall colours spans by LLM / Tool / Memory / Gateway / HTTP / Agent / Other, and the legend lists only the categories this trace has (here LLM, Tool, Memory, HTTP, Agent); a tool span's row shows the tool name (kb_search; the full span name is execute_tool kb_search). The structure of this trace in this lab (durations on the right):

text
POST /invocations                                   89s
├─ Bedrock AgentCore.ListEvents ×3                  69–86ms   ← read short-term memory
├─ Bedrock AgentCore.RetrieveMemoryRecords ×2       260–264ms ← read long-term memory
└─ invoke_agent Strands Agents                      88s
   ├─ execute_event_loop_cycle                      8.5s
   │  ├─ chat → chat global.zai.glm-5.3             8.0s      ← first model call, decides to retrieve (in 12,822 · out 484)
   │  └─ kb_search ×2 → Bedrock Agent Runtime.Retrieve  440–470ms ← two parallel retrievals from lab-unicorn-policies
   ├─ execute_event_loop_cycle                      14.8s
   │  ├─ chat → chat global.zai.glm-5.3             14.8s     ← second, decides to fetch the current time (in 3,958 · out 1,321)
   │  └─ current_utc_time                           <1ms
   ├─ execute_event_loop_cycle                      64.5s
   │  └─ chat → chat global.zai.glm-5.3             64.5s     ← third, writes the final answer (in 18,488 · out 1,259)
   └─ Bedrock AgentCore.CreateEvent ×2              87–104ms  ← write this turn back to memory

Compare the chat and tool durations first. Here the three model calls total 87 seconds, while the two parallel retrievals took about 0.5 seconds and the time lookup under 1 millisecond: the time goes into model generation, not retrieval. The third call produced 1,259 output tokens in 64.5 seconds, about 20 tokens per second; at a faster hour the same question finishes in a dozen seconds. If a tool span were clearly longer, you would look at retrieval or the gateway. The Span card to the right of the waterfall shows the first failed span, or the first model-category span when nothing failed (here the first chat); click any row to switch to it. Click the last chat global.zai.glm-5.3: the card shows Span chat global.zai.glm-5.3, Model global.zai.glm-5.3, Provider aws.bedrock, Finish reason end_turn, Starts at +24s, Duration 65s, Status UNSET · http 200, a Tokens section with Input 18,488, Output 1,259, Cache read / write 0 / 0, Est. cost ≈$0.038, and Attributes · 32 below (Show all expands the raw attributes). This span records no message content, so the Input · N messages / Output · N messages sections do not appear (frontend/src/v3/pages/observability/TraceView.tsx renders them only when the span carries messages).

Input tokens far outnumber output: every model call carries the system prompt, the earlier turns and the retrieved policy snippets, so later calls carry more input (in the table in section 1 this question's whole trace is 38,332 tokens). Click the invoke_agent Strands Agents row and its card also records 13,184 cache-read tokens: the part of the prompt that hit the model-side cache.

When system traces exist, the Traces tab shows a Show N system traces checkbox (the two-span InternalOperation health checks a managed Harness runtime emits). There were none in this lab's 24 hours, so the checkbox did not appear (frontend/src/v3/pages/observability/Lists.tsx shows it only when systemCount is above 0).

Telemetry is per endpoint

Every AgentCore endpoint writes its own log group (…-<endpoint>) and service name (….<endpoint>). In gated mode:

Traffic Endpoint Where you see it
Chat, public API (/v1/...), online evaluation, scheduled regression runs live The service name in the trace header's small line ends in .live
The release evaluation of a candidate (the Evaluate and Release chapters) candidate Service ends in .candidate

The rule the platform applies: a run pinned to an endpoint reads that endpoint; a gated agent reads live; everything else reads DEFAULT. The dashboards, online evaluation and insights therefore show the endpoint your users actually talk to, not an idle DEFAULT. In this lab only lab-service-assistant is on dual endpoints (service lab_service_assistant_de2323.live); lab-policy-advisor never went through the gate and its traces carry the service harness_lab_policy_advisor.DEFAULT.

Expected result: the header's small line reads lab-service-assistant · … · lab_service_assistant_de2323.live (the service ends in .live; the runtime suffix differs per environment); the waterfall has both chat global.zai.glm-5.3 and kb_search spans, and the Span card shows their tokens and estimated cost.

5. Put a number on tokens and cost (admin)

Sign in as admin (administrators see every module by default) and open rail Modules → Agent runtime → Spend & alerts (/v3/costs). Only administrators see this entry, and GET /api/costs is admin-only.

In the image: 1 tiles: Est. spend · 24H, Month to date, Tokens, Agents with traffic; 2 the basis toggle Estimate / Billed; 3 By agent, one <runtime>.<endpoint> per row; 4 By project; 5 By person: Unattributed (API or evaluation) and developer; 6 the 1h–30d window.

The Spend tab (the header switches between Spend and Alerts, and the Estimate / Billed toggle to its left picks the cost basis):

  • The page opens with a watch summary; with no alert rules yet it reads "Nothing is watched yet — add a threshold to be told when spend, errors or latency move.", and All rules next to it jumps to the Alerts tab.
  • Tiles: Est. spend · 24H ("Estimate, from the price map"), Month to date ("estimated, this workspace"), Tokens, Agents with traffic. Below them pick a window (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d); Re-read bypasses the cache, and the right side says how long ago it was computed. In this lab for 24h: $2.61, month to date $11.02 (the whole workspace's running total this month, every earlier lab included), 1,188,345 tokens, 7 agents.
  • By agent: attributed from the runtime service name on each span, one row per <runtime>.<endpoint> with estimated cost, Tokens and Model calls. lab-service-assistant takes the top three rows: lab_service_assistant_de2323.candidate ($1.32 · 616,056 · 202, the gate's evaluations of candidate versions), lab_service_assistant_de2323.DEFAULT ($0.83 · 384,674 · 141, the calls before the Release chapter moved it onto dual endpoints, including the Evaluate chapter's dev run) and lab_service_assistant_de2323.live ($0.25 · 126,024 · 19, the chat in section 1). The other rows are the endpoints of lab-canary-sandbox (stable9b543e / treat9b543e are the two arms of the Release chapter's canary, DEFAULT its own chat) and lab-policy-advisor (harness_lab_policy_advisor.DEFAULT, $0.03).
  • By project: one row per project with agents with traffic and tokens. Here only retail-service ($2.61 · 7 · 1,188,345).
  • By person: console sessions attributed to who started them, with Person and Sessions. Here developer is $0.22 over 5 sessions (the chat in section 1).
  • Unattributed (API or evaluation): public API calls and evaluation runs have no console session and get their own row in By person (here $2.39 over 198 sessions).

Estimate is model tokens × the price map, available within minutes; Billed reads what AWS actually charged per launchpad:project tag from Cost Explorer, up to a day late and including infrastructure. The cost allocation tag must first be activated under Configuration → Cost tags, and cost from before activation is listed as untagged. This lab only uses Estimate.

The Alerts tab: an administrator can create a New rule whose What to watch is Error rate, p95 latency, Online quality or Spend this month, with an https Webhook (optional) (notified once when the rule goes from ok to firing). Rules are readable by every member and writable by administrators only. Still as admin, create one rule that mirrors criterion P2:

  1. Switch to Alerts on the right of the page header. The page shows four tiles, Firing, Close to the line, Unknown and Rules, and "No rules yet.". Click New rule.
  2. In the "New alert rule" dialog: What to watch p95 latency (hint: "95th percentile end-to-end latency, in milliseconds."); Name lab-p95-30s; Fire when above ms 30000; Window left at 24h (choices 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d); Webhook (optional) empty. Click Create.

In the image: 1 What to watch: p95 latency; 2 Name lab-p95-30s; 3 Fire when above ms: 30000; 4 Window stays 24h; 5 click Create (Webhook left empty).

  1. Expected result: the toast "Rule created", and a new lab-p95-30s card reading "p95 latency above 30000 ms · 24h", state Unknown and "not checked yet"; Unknown and Rules both become 1.
  2. Click Re-check now; the toast reads "Re-checked · 1 firing". The card turns Firing with last value 32254 ms (the dashboard's P95 of 32s) and detail p95 over 413 traces; the Firing tile reads 1 and Unknown drops back to 0. The rule fires because the last 24 hours' P95 is above criterion P2's 30 seconds, the same reason the Release chapter requested a waiver for P2: a waiver lets this release through, it does not change the latency in production, and the alert still reports it. When P95 drops back below 30000 ms the rule returns to OK; with a webhook it notifies once, on the change from ok to firing (backend/app/services/alerts.py).

In the image: 1 tiles: Firing 1, Close to the line 0, Unknown 0, Rules 1; 2 Re-check now; 3 the rule card: p95 latency above 30000 ms · 24h, Firing after the check, last value 32254 ms, detail "p95 over 413 traces".

In your environment P95 depends on how fast the model is that day: below 30 seconds the card shows OK. Either result shows the rule working.

Leave the rule in place; section 2.2 of the Clean-up chapter deletes it.

6. Intent view: what are people asking

Back in the biz-owner window, click rail Modules → Agent evaluation → Intent view (/v3/intents). Leave the range on the right of the page header at 7 days (also: 1, 14, 30 days) and change the agent picker from All agents to lab-service-assistant.

How to read the page:

  • The intent view groups by each session's first message, counting a session once: section 1's five questions share one session, grouped by its first message "I bought Bluetooth earbuds at the Unicorn Mall…"; the lab-policy-advisor session is grouped by "Flash-sale…".
  • Tiles: Sessions, Intents, Unanswered, Most disliked intent.
  • Questions it could not answer: refusals, empty answers and errors, each row with Send to issue box and Open session.
  • What people asked: columns Intent, Sessions, Thumbs-down rate, Unanswered, and View N at the end of each row opens that group's sessions. Normally an AI model (backend/app/services/intents.py) names the intents in business language, in the language of the UI.

Expected result (measured in this lab, lab-service-assistant, 7 days, about 4 seconds after Regroup):

  • The title "5 things people came to do"; Sessions 9, Intents 5 (with "Grouped by an AI model from each session's first message." below), Unanswered 0, Most disliked intent — (nobody has given a thumbs-down yet).
  • Questions it could not answer reads "Nothing went unanswered in this window.".
  • What people asked has 5 rows (group names from one run, sessions): Calculate flight ticket refund amount 3, Calculate partial refund with discount proration 3, Return policy question for unactivated item 1, Save personal travel and shopping preferences 1, Travel booking advice based on preferences 1. Section 1's session is in Return policy question for unactivated item (its first message is the earbuds return); the others are questions from earlier chapters.
  • The model judges group names and Unanswered afresh each time: besides the rules for empty answers, errors and refusal phrases, it also marks a session that did not really answer the question as unanswered (backend/app/services/intents.py). One grouping of the same 9 sessions in the Chinese UI also made 5 groups, cut differently (for example 商城部分退货退款计算 (mall partial refund calculation) 3, 商城退货政策咨询 (mall return policy question) 1).

In the image: 1 the agent picker set to lab-service-assistant; 2 Regroup; 3 tiles: Sessions 9, Intents 5 (grouped by an AI model from each session's first message), Unanswered 0; 4 Questions it could not answer: none in this window; 5 What people asked: Calculate flight ticket refund amount 3, Calculate partial refund with discount proration 3 and three more (group names from one run).

Switch the picker to lab-policy-advisor (12 sessions) and section 1's "Flash-sale…" session lands in a coupon-stacking group (one run named it 商城优惠券满减叠加咨询 (mall coupon and threshold-discount stacking), 1 session). Questions it could not answer has 8 rows, mostly sessions from earlier chapters where the Harness runtime raised an error (the answer reads RuntimeClientError: … or EventStreamError: …), plus two where the advisor found no basis in the knowledge base and declined outright ("cannot confirm your personal hotel preferences", "cannot give a confirmed answer"). These are exactly the sessions worth sending to the issue box.

All agents (28 sessions in this lab) is AI-grouped too: after Regroup the four tiles show — first, and the more sessions the longer the wait (tens of seconds here). The result is cached on the server for 10 minutes, and reopening the page within that time shows the cached result. One run read "9 questions went unanswered", Sessions 28, Intents 12, Unanswered 9, and the top groups of What people asked were Flight ticket refund amount calculation 7, Flight cancellation affecting hotel refund 6, Assistant self introduction 3, Partial order refund calculation 3. The same sessions that the lab-service-assistant run called "Calculate flight ticket refund amount" are "Flight ticket refund amount calculation" here: group names change on every call.

This is one of the doors into the Improve chapter: the business owner spots a problem here and works it in the issue box and admission queue.

7. Policy decision logs (admin)

In the Release chapter admin attached a policy engine to the shared launchpad-gw, wrote Cedar policies, collected evidence with Policy test and finally switched to ENFORCE. Still as admin, open rail Modules → Agent runtime → Governance (/v3/governance); on the Gateways tab, in the Policy decisions card (last 24h) the launchpad-gw row reads launchpad_gw_<gateway id suffix>_policy · ENFORCE, with Allowed 2 and Denied 6 in this lab; click Decisions on that row. It opens the gateway detail page hosted inside V3 (address /v2/governance?view=gateway&gateway=…&section=decisions), already on its Decisions section.

  • At the top: Time range (default Last 24 hours) and a Policy filter (default All).
  • KPI tiles, in order: Decisions, LOG_ONLY evidence ("what the cutover gate counts"), Allowed, Denied. In this lab: 8, 3, 2, 6.
  • Evidence breakdown (source: CloudWatch policy metrics) splits by operation, enforcement mode and policy. In this lab: By operation AuthorizeAction 2 allowed / 6 denied; By enforcement mode ENFORCE 2 / 3, LOG_ONLY 0 / 3; By policy unicorn_payout_admin_only-… 0 / 3, unicorn_tool_allowlist-… 2 / 0. The note below says the breakdowns are not a decomposition of the total (AWS publishes the policy dimension only for decisions that had a determining policy, and the tool dimension only for per-tool authorization), so the two By policy rows adding up to 5 rather than the 8 Decisions is expected (the 3 LOG_ONLY decisions had no determining policy).
  • Policy decisions rows come from Policy spans and are sampled. This lab shows "No per-decision rows (Policy spans) in this window" and "Gateway tracing is not configured (delivery_source_missing). Configure trace delivery for this Gateway, then generate new traffic; tracing is not retroactive.": the workshop template does not configure trace delivery for launchpad-gw; the counts above are unaffected.
  • With no decision at all in the window, the tiles read 0 and the page says "No policy decisions in this window." (frontend/src/v2/pages/governance/Decisions.tsx); widening Time range to Last 7 days brings back the Release chapter's policy tests. This lab had 8 decisions in 24 hours, so that did not occur.

The Audit section next to it is the gateway's immutable change log.

8. Drift watch: re-apply the standard on a schedule

A model can change under an agent without a line of code changing. A standard checked only at release time stops being a standard within weeks. The drift watch replays the golden set's regression split against live on a schedule and scores it with the same criteria table.

As developer open rail Modules → Agent evaluation → Standards, pick lab-service-assistant in the agent picker on the right of the page header, and click the Drift watch sub-tab (/v3/standards?agent=<id>&view=watch). From top to bottom the page shows Alerts, Pass rate against its baseline, Agent or judge?, Schedule and Scheduled runs.

In the image: 1 Alerts: "Nothing firing across the last N run(s), checked …"; 2 Pass rate against its baseline (Quality by default, the dashed line is the rolling median); 3 Agent or judge?: agent versions in this window, 4 judges needing recalibration; 4 Schedule: Daily, 3, 1, 5, Enabled, On, next run at the next 03:00 UTC; 5 Scheduled runs: the last row is the regression run that Run now added.

Before you save a schedule, this lab's page reads: Alerts 0, "Nothing firing across the last N run(s), checked …"; all three dimensions of Pass rate against its baseline already have an 8-point baseline; the Schedule card is tagged Not scheduled and Run now is greyed out (it cannot be clicked before a schedule exists, frontend/src/v3/pages/standards/Watch.tsx); Scheduled runs already lists the dev, regression and holdout runs from the Evaluate and Release chapters (agent versions 2, 3, 4, criteria version v1). The table lists every run of this agent against this criteria table, not only scheduled ones, so the Release chapter's gate runs have already filled the baseline.

Fill in the Schedule card:

Field Value Notes
How often Daily Weekly is the other option
At hour (UTC) 3 0–23
Repeats (k) 1 Above 1 the cost multiplies on every run
Cost ceiling (USD) 5 (the confirm amount set in the Roles chapter) A run estimated above it is skipped and reported, rather than spent
Enabled checked

Click Save at the bottom of the card ("Schedule saved"); the card's tag changes from Not scheduled to On and "Next run <date> 03:00" (the next 03:00 UTC) appears below. Then click Run now next to it ("Run started"); the line becomes "Next run <date> 03:00 · Last run queued — run <run id>". It still says "Last run queued" after the run finishes: last_status only records queued and skipped-for-cost, and the outcome is in the Scheduled runs table.

Saving the schedule pins the criteria table's currently published version to the watch. When the table later publishes a new version, come back and click Save again so the watch picks it up (the Improve chapter relies on this).

In this lab the run (task watch regression <date>, description scheduled re-evaluation (developer), 15 regression items, 4 evaluators) took 7 min 32 s and cost $0.55 actual ($0.58 estimated); averages Builtin.Correctness 1.00, unicorn_fee_check 1.00, unicorn_privacy_guard 0.93, unicorn_no_overpromise 0.93. Refresh the page and read the panels:

  • Alerts: each family is judged its own way. Count (red-line violations, evaluation errors) uses an absolute threshold and Pages immediately; Score waits until the baseline has 8 or more points, and otherwise says "Too little history to judge a drop in: …"; Distribution compares how the intent mix moved and names the slice that moved. When nothing fires, the page says so explicitly, "Nothing firing across the last N run(s), checked …": "no alert" is itself an output, so a stopped watch is not misread as fourteen calm days. In this lab every dimension's baseline is long enough, and the result is "Nothing firing across the last 11 run(s)" (this run included; your count depends on how many runs the earlier chapters made).
  • Pass rate against its baseline: pick a dimension at the top right of the card (only dimensions with data are listed; Quality by default); the dashed line is the rolling median of the preceding runs. This lab offers Cognition, Quality and Responsibility; this run's Quality is 1.00 (baseline 1.00) and Responsibility 0.93 (baseline 0.94), neither below its baseline.
  • Agent or judge?: a dip can be the agent getting worse or the judge changing its mind. It lists Agent versions in this window and Judges needing recalibration, with a table below of each judge criterion's Calibrated state and κ; a version change is flagged in amber, and the card opens with "Re-run the frozen calibration set: if the judge now disagrees with the human labels, it is judge drift, not an agent regression.". In this lab: Agent versions in this window 2, 3, 4 (amber), Judges needing recalibration 4; the table has C1 Builtin.Correctness, Q1 unicorn_fee_check-… and S1 unicorn_privacy_guard-… as Never calibrated, and S2 unicorn_no_overpromise-… as Found not aligned with κ 1.00 (the Evaluate chapter's calibration samples all carried the same label, so κ is recorded as 1.00 by convention but the judge is found not aligned).
  • Scheduled runs: time, split, agent version and criteria version per run; click a row to open the evaluation task detail.

Expected result: Schedule shows On; Scheduled runs ends with a new row <first 8 of the run id> · <time> · regression · 4 · v1; Alerts is 0.

Scheduled runs invoke the agent and evaluators every day and cost money. At the end of the workshop come back, uncheck Enabled and Save (the Cleanup chapter reminds you too).

9. Scorecard and decision history

Scorecard (business owner)

In the biz-owner window open Standards, pick lab-service-assistant in the header, and you land on the Scorecard sub-tab (view=scorecard). This is the page a business owner reads (readings below are after section 8's run finished):

  • Needs attention: the things a person has to act on, listed first. In this lab 2 rows, both Waiting: "4 judge criteria are not calibrated and only observe" (link Calibration on the right) and "2 waivers are in force" (link Release gate: the Release chapter's P2 and K1).
  • Are we meeting the standard we signed: tiles Standard v1 (signed by biz-owner), Last release verdict PASS ("Released · <time>", the Release chapter's last signature), Uncalibrated judges 4 ("These criteria are on record but do not block a release."), Alerts firing 0 ("Nothing firing"). Below them, five dimension tiles: Cognition 100.0%, Quality 100.0%, Responsibility 93.3% (all three read "Standard —" and "0 of N gates in effect": their criteria are uncalibrated judges that only observe, and the small line is the pass rate across runs); Cost 5,778 in red ("tokens per session <= 500 · n = 15", K1 passes on its waiver); Performance 13,502 (two rows "latency P95 (ms) <= 120,000 · n = 15" and "<= 30,000 · n = 15", for P1 and P2). n = 15 shows the tiles read the latest run, section 8's drift-watch run. A dimension nobody wrote a criterion for reads "Not applicable — nobody wrote a criterion here"; every dimension in this table has one, so it does not appear.
  • Release card: Production version 4, Endpoints live / candidate dual endpoints, Last run the time of section 8's drift-watch run.
  • What the standard still owes: C1, Q1, S1 as Uncalibrated judge · Never calibrated, S2 as Uncalibrated judge · Found not aligned (the Evaluate chapter's verdict; not aligned does not count as calibrated), and K1, P2 as Waiver in force · biz-owner · <expiry date>.
  • Coverage: a criterion × case-tier matrix (Known good / Known bad / Ambiguous / Adversarial / Samples); in this lab P1, P2, K1 have 48 each, C1 41, Q1 18, S2 17, and S1 only 5 adversarial samples.

In the image: 1 Needs attention: "4 judge criteria are not calibrated…" and "2 waivers are in force"; 2 Standard v1 (biz-owner), Last release verdict PASS, Uncalibrated judges 4, Alerts firing 0; 3 five dimensions: Cognition 100.0%, Quality 100.0%, Responsibility 93.3%, Cost 5,778, Performance 13,502 (after the drift-watch run, n = 15); 4 Release (production version 4, live / candidate dual endpoints) and What the standard still owes (C1, Q1, S1, S2 and the K1, P2 waivers).

Decision history (administrator)

Switch to the Decision history sub-tab (view=audit). It answers who signed the standard, who admitted a sample, who approved a waiver and who released; filter above the table by All decisions / Criteria / Golden set / Calibration / Releases / Waivers; the columns are When, Who, What and On.

The endpoint behind it, GET /api/audit, is administrators only: opened as biz-owner, the table reads "This needs an administrator." (the endpoint returns 403 auth.forbidden). Look at it in the admin window.

The page shows only records whose subject contains the current agent's ID, and the Standards header always has an agent selected, so only agent-subject records appear. In this lab admin sees 6 rows (newest first; <id> in the subject is lab-service-assistant's agent ID):

Who What On
developer POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/release/sign /api/agents/<id>/release/sign [auth.permission_required]
release-ops release.rollback <id>
developer waiver.request <id>:P2
developer waiver.request <id>:K1
release-ops release.migrate_live <id>
developer POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/release/migrate /api/agents/<id>/release/migrate [auth.permission_required]

Rows whose action is POST /api/… and whose subject ends in [auth.permission_required] are refused attempts: developer trying to switch to dual endpoints in the Evaluate chapter and to sign the release in the Release chapter were both stopped with 403, and the platform records the attempt in the decision history too.

Signing the criteria table, seeding the golden set, calibration, approving waivers, release evaluation and signing have the criteria table, golden set, annotation task, waiver and release record IDs as their subjects and do not appear in this table. To see the full history, admin opens <ConsoleUrl>/api/audit?limit=50 in the browser and reads the raw JSON (field events). In order from Define to Release the chain is: criteria.sign (biz-owner, criteria table v1), golden.seed (biz-owner), release.migrate_live (release-ops), release.evaluate (developer, one per gate run), calibration.not_aligned (biz-owner, the S2 verdict), waiver.request ×2 (developer), waiver.approve ×2 (release-ops), release.sign (release-ops), release.rollback (release-ops), then another release.evaluate and release.sign, with the refused attempts above in between. The raw log also holds entries unrelated to the agent, such as an administrator deleting annotation tasks (annotation.delete) and system updates (system.update.*). Saving the schedule and Run now in section 8 write no decision record.

In the image: 1 the agent selected in the header, lab-service-assistant; 2 the Decision history sub-tab; 3 filters: All decisions / Criteria / Golden set / Calibration / Releases / Waivers; 4 the table: the refused sign attempt, release.rollback, two waiver.request, release.migrate_live, the refused migrate attempt.

Checklist

  • The observability dashboard's Sessions and Tokens show data; Tools has kb_search and …___AgenticRetrieveStream
  • A session detail shows the conversation replay and Traces in this session
  • The waterfall shows chat global.zai.glm-5.3 and kb_search spans with tokens and estimated cost
  • developer scored a session once with Score now (Builtin.Helpfulness + unicorn_privacy_guard)
  • The service name in the trace header ends in .live (production traffic in gated mode)
  • The Governance Decisions section shows denies under ENFORCE, counted under unicorn_payout_admin_only-…
  • admin sees estimated spend by agent, by project and by person in Spend & alerts and created the alert rule lab-p95-30s, which reads Firing or OK after Re-check now (depending on the day's P95)
  • Intent view with lab-service-assistant picked is grouped by the AI, and section 1's session is in the return-policy group
  • The Drift watch of lab-service-assistant is scheduled and one regression run completed
  • biz-owner reads the Scorecard; admin reads the Decision history and the full record at /api/audit

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
Every observability view is empty CloudWatch Transaction Search is not enabled Re-check it in the Setup chapter
No trace right after chatting The spans have not landed yet (all visible within 2.5 minutes in this lab) Wait, then Refresh
Everyone else's agents are listed, but one agent never appears in the Sessions / Traces agent drop-down, even after 5+ minutes The drop-down does not read the agent list; it lists only agents with spans in the current time range. The usual case is an agent deployed as a BYOC Code zip (such as lab-legacy-agent): the platform injects no ADOT, so it chats but emits no spans Check whether the agent page shows BYOC above the title; if so, follow B.4 at the end of section 3, option B in the Build chapter — rebuild with Strands / a container, or switch to Dockerfile build and instrument it yourself. If it is not BYOC, make sure the time range covers the call and that you actually invoked it in Chat
Numbers change only after a while 60-second cache Refresh bypasses it
Cost shows — Model missing from the price map Administrator clicks Update prices (members without write access do not see the button)
Score now: "No span records found for this session in the selected time range yet." Spans not landed yet, or the range is too narrow Widen the range and retry
A session or trace detail says "This session was not found in the selected range." / "This trace …" The range starts after the session Go back to the list, widen the range to 7D and open it again
The trace service ends in .DEFAULT The agent is not on gated live / candidate endpoints Check the release policy is gated and the release stage finished
Drift watch Run now is greyed out The schedule was never saved (the console disables the button without a schedule; calling the API directly returns watch.not_configured) Click Save first
watch.over_cost_ceiling Estimate above the Cost ceiling Raise the ceiling or lower Repeats
watch.no_golden / watch.empty_split No golden set serves the criteria, or the regression split has no active items Check the golden set's criteria link and regression split (the Evaluate chapter; regression should hold 15 items)
The drift watch Alerts show a count alert 1 evaluation error(s) In that run one session holds a repeated answer (one call stalled upstream and was sent again); the judges that compare with the expected answer have none for the extra trace and record an evaluation error, and count alerts page on any absolute count. It stays in the alert window until no run in the window has an evaluation error
The alert rule lab-p95-30s is Firing right after the check The last 24 hours' P95 is above 30 seconds, the same reason the Release chapter waived P2 (31,965 ms in this lab) That is the rule working. To see OK, raise the threshold to 60000 for a moment and re-check
biz-owner gets a permission error on Decision history GET /api/audit is admin-only Use admin
Online evaluation or Governance is missing from the rail In a fresh window a member account shows the everyday modules only Click Show every module at the bottom of Modules
Intent view tiles stay at — after Regroup The AI grouping has not returned yet (slower with more sessions: about 4 s for lab-service-assistant and 16–76 s for All agents in this lab) Wait for it, or pick a specific agent; if the AI call fails the page shows the amber notice "The AI grouping was unavailable…" and falls back to mechanical grouping (backend/app/services/intents.py)
Decision history has rows whose action starts with POST /api/… and whose subject ends in [auth.permission_required] They are refused attempts (for example developer trying to sign a release), which the platform records too Nothing to do; they show the separation of duties at work
Decision history lacks criteria.sign and similar records The table only shows records about the current agent Open <ConsoleUrl>/api/audit?limit=50 as admin
